steps.sop: The Software Engineer splits any story above the team's split threshold (e.g. 13 points) or converts it to a time-boxed spike in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; items with wide estimate spread or unresolved dependencies are flagged 'needs-spike' and deferred with a note, excluded from the sprint and returned to refinement with an owner and target date. Done when no oversized item remains unaddressed.
steps.verify: Query stories above the split threshold; pass if each is split or linked to a spike, and every 'needs-spike' item shows an owner and target refinement date.

steps.title: Reconcile the queue to zero unestimated items
steps.sop: The Software Engineer reconciles the session output: the count of estimated items equals the 'Ready for estimation' queue, and every in-scope item has a non-zero point value at session end. Done when the unestimated count is 0.
steps.verify: Compare the queue count to estimated count in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; pass if they match and no in-scope item has zero or missing points.

steps.title: Record the session summary in the sprint-planning notes
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records the estimation results (points per story, planning-poker outcome, date, participant list) in the sprint-planning notes. Done when the summary is saved and dated.
steps.verify: Open the sprint-planning notes; pass if the session date, participants, and per-story outcomes are recorded and match the values in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps.

steps.title: Obtain Scrum Master sign-off on the estimation round
steps.sop: The Scrum Master signs off the estimation round; exceptions to the Definition of Ready are recorded for Product Owner decision within the sprint. Done when PASS criteria hold: 100% of in-scope items estimated and DoR-compliant, no story above the split threshold without a split/spike.
steps.verify: Open the sign-off record; pass if the Scrum Master approval is present and any DoR exception carries a pending or completed Product Owner decision.

steps.title: Stand up the SIT environment on the release-candidate build
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer deploys the RC build tagged in the release pipeline of the source code/CI-CD repository into the SIT environment; the cycle window is 3 business days from RC freeze to sign-off. Done when SIT runs the tagged RC build.
steps.verify: Open the SIT deployment record in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if the deployed build number matches the RC tag and the deployment date starts the 3-day window.

steps.title: Execute the integration and system test suites
steps.sop: The QA Automation Engineer executes all integration test suites plus the end-to-end system scenarios covering the Guidewire PolicyCenter/ClaimCenter integration surface via the source code/CI-CD repository pipeline; the regression subset also runs nightly. Done when every planned suite has run against the RC.
steps.verify: Open the pipeline run history; pass if all planned suites show executions against the RC build within the cycle window.

steps.title: Record a status on every planned test case
steps.sop: The QA Analyst records Pass/Fail/Blocked on every planned test case, memorialized in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps. Done when 100% of cases are executed with 0 in 'Not Run' at cycle close.
steps.verify: Open the cycle's case list in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; pass if every case shows a recorded status and the 'Not Run' count is 0.

steps.title: Raise a linked defect for each failure
steps.sop: The QA Analyst raises a defect (type 'Bug', linked to the failing test case) in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps for every failure; blockers gate the release. Done when no failed case lacks a linked defect.
steps.verify: Query failed cases in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; pass if each links a Bug and every blocker is marked as release-gating.

steps.title: Reconcile executed counts and the pass-rate gate
steps.sop: The Test Lead reconciles executed count to planned count (planned = executed + explicitly deferred with approval) and checks the gates: pass rate >= 98% and 0 open critical/blocker defects at sign-off. Done when the reconciliation and gate results are recorded.
steps.verify: Open the cycle summary; pass if planned = executed + approved deferrals, pass rate >= 98%, and no critical/blocker defect remains open.

steps.title: Log deferred cases as approved exceptions
steps.sop: The Test Lead logs any deferred case as an 'SDLC-Exception' in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps with Test Lead + Product Owner approval and a target fix release. Done when every deferral carries both approvals.
steps.verify: Open each deferral's exception; pass if it shows Test Lead and Product Owner approval plus a named target fix release.

steps.title: Archive the execution report as a build artifact
steps.sop: The QA Automation Engineer archives the test execution report (JUnit XML + summary) as a build artifact in the source code/CI-CD repository keyed to the RC build number, stamped with build SHA, environment, and timestamp, retained 400 days. Done when the artifact is archived with all stamps.
steps.verify: Open the build artifacts for the RC; pass if the JUnit XML and summary exist, keyed to the RC number with SHA/environment/timestamp and 400-day retention.

steps.title: Obtain Test Lead sign-off on the cycle
steps.sop: The Test Lead signs off the completed cycle in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps. Done when the sign-off is recorded within the 3-business-day window with results attached.
steps.verify: Open the cycle record; pass if the Test Lead sign-off is present, dated inside the window, and references the archived results.

tasks.taskName: Execute test cases against release candidate

steps.title: Assemble the RC test scope in the Xray/Zephyr test plan
steps.sop: The QA Analyst assembles the test plan in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps (Xray/Zephyr): 100% of regression cases for changed components plus all new-feature acceptance cases tagged to the release epic — risk-based full run with no sampling on critical paths. Done when the plan contains the complete case set.
steps.verify: Open the test plan in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; pass if every regression case for changed components and every new-feature case is included and tagged to the release epic.

steps.title: Freeze executions to the RC build
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records the RC freeze on the plan: only executions against the frozen RC build count (RC freeze date to go/no-go, e.g. 2026-06-28 to 2026-07-02); any code change requires a new RC and re-execution — prior results expire. Done when the RC build id and window are stamped on the plan.
steps.verify: Open the plan header; pass if the frozen RC build id and window dates are recorded and no execution references a different build.

steps.title: Execute cases with complete execution records
steps.sop: The QA Analyst (with the Backend Developer and UI Developer) executes each case, recording build/version under test, tester, timestamp, status (pass/fail/blocked), and defect link on failure in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; executions missing build id or status are re-run. Done when every case has a complete execution record.
steps.verify: Sample execution records in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; pass if each shows build id, tester, timestamp, status, and — for failures — a defect link.

steps.title: Raise and triage a Bug per failure
steps.sop: The QA Analyst raises a Bug in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps linked to each failed test case and triages severity; blocked cases record the blocker reason. Done when no failure lacks a triaged Bug.
steps.verify: Query failed and blocked cases; pass if every failure links a severity-triaged Bug and every blocked case states its blocker reason.

steps.title: Attach the automated run logs to the test plan
steps.sop: The Software Engineer exports the automated run logs (JUnit XML) from the CI pipeline and attaches them to the Xray test plan in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps with the RC version tag; retained per release evidence policy. Done when the logs are attached and tagged.
steps.verify: Open the test plan attachments; pass if the JUnit XML logs are present, tagged with the RC version, and match the executed automated cases.

steps.title: Reconcile the execution ledger to zero not-run
steps.sop: The QA Analyst reconciles counts: planned test cases = passed + failed + blocked + skipped-with-reason, with no case left 'not run' at go/no-go. Done when the delta is 0.
steps.verify: Open the plan summary in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; pass if the four-way count reconciliation balances exactly and the not-run count is 0.

steps.title: Apply the release gates and log unfixed failures
steps.sop: The Software Engineer applies the gates: 100% of critical/high-priority cases pass, >= 98% overall pass rate, 0 open critical/high defects; unresolved criticals block go-live unless the Release Manager approves an 'SDLC-Exception', and failures not fixed pre-release are logged as 'SDLC-Exception' with risk disposition (owner = QA Lead, 10-business-day SLA). Done when the gate outcome and any exceptions are recorded.
steps.verify: Open the gate record; pass if the three thresholds are evidenced, and every unfixed failure carries an approved exception with owner and disposition.

steps.title: Obtain Test Lead sign-off with evidence linked
steps.sop: The Test Lead signs off the RC test results and the evidence URL (the Xray/Zephyr test plan with execution records and logs) is recorded on the release go/no-go record. Done when sign-off and the evidence link are both in place.
steps.verify: Open the go/no-go record; pass if the Test Lead sign-off is present and the recorded URL resolves to the completed test plan.

steps.title: Confirm UAT scenario coverage in the traceability matrix
steps.sop: The QA Analyst confirms in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps that every in-scope story requiring business validation has UAT scenarios mapped to its business acceptance criteria in the traceability matrix. Done when no in-scope story lacks a mapped scenario.
steps.verify: Open the traceability matrix in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; pass if every in-scope story maps to >=1 UAT scenario tied to its acceptance criteria.

steps.title: Schedule named business stakeholders for the UAT window
steps.sop: The Business Analyst schedules the named business stakeholders to execute in the UAT environment during the release UAT window (typically the final sprint before go-live). Done when every scenario has a named tester and slot.
steps.verify: Open the UAT schedule; pass if each scenario shows a named business tester and a date inside the UAT window.

steps.title: Execute scenarios and record outcomes
steps.sop: The QA Analyst oversees execution, recording per case in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps: scenario, tester, execution date, actual vs expected result, and pass/fail — expected results trace to the story acceptance criteria, not free interpretation. Done when no case lacks a recorded outcome.
steps.verify: Open the executed cases; pass if every case shows tester, date, actual-vs-expected, and pass/fail, with expected results referencing the story criteria.

steps.title: Raise severity-rated defects for failures
steps.sop: The QA Analyst raises a defect in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps with severity for each failed case; Critical/High block sign-off, while Medium/Low may be deferred only with a Product Owner-approved risk note and target release. Done when every failure has a rated, dispositioned defect.
steps.verify: Query UAT defects; pass if each failed case links a severity-rated defect and every deferral shows the Product Owner risk note and target release.

steps.title: Reconcile executed against planned UAT counts
steps.sop: The QA Analyst reconciles executed vs planned UAT case counts and pass/fail tallies in the traceability matrix. Done when executed equals planned minus signed waivers, and unexecuted cases are 0 or explicitly waived with business sign-off.
steps.verify: Open the matrix tallies; pass if executed = planned - signed waivers and every waiver carries business sign-off.

steps.title: Escalate blocking defects to hold the go-live gate
steps.sop: The Business Analyst escalates blocking defects to the Product Owner and Release Manager; the go-live gate is held until each is resolved or formally risk-accepted. Done when no unresolved blocker lacks an escalation record.
steps.verify: Open the escalation records; pass if every open Critical/High defect shows an escalation and a resolution or formal risk acceptance before gate release.

steps.title: Capture the signed acceptance form on the release version
steps.sop: The QA Analyst captures the UAT results, defects, and the signed acceptance form on the release version in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps, timestamped and version-stamped, retained per release records policy — sign-off is valid for this release version only. Done when the evidence set is attached.
steps.verify: Open the release version; pass if results, defects, and the signed form are attached with timestamps and the correct release version reference.

steps.title: Obtain Product Owner sign-off on UAT completion
steps.sop: The Product Owner signs off UAT in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps. Done when PASS criteria hold: 100% of UAT cases executed with recorded outcomes and 0 open Critical/High defects.
steps.verify: Open the sign-off record; pass if the Product Owner approval is present and the final tallies show full execution and no open Critical/High defect.

steps.title: Publish the workshop charter in Confluence
steps.sop: The Business Analyst publishes the workshop charter in Confluence defining the in-scope value stream/application and the named SMEs from affected business units, citing the BA Playbook v2.1 facilitation method and the discovery window (e.g. 3-week discovery per the initiative plan). Done when the charter is published with scope, SMEs, and method version.
steps.verify: Open the charter in Confluence; pass if scope, named SMEs, discovery dates, and the BA Playbook v2.1 citation are all present.

steps.title: Run each discovery workshop session
steps.sop: The Business Analyst facilitates each scheduled session with the SMEs, capturing the current-state process and pain points; the Backend Developer supports on system specifics. Done when every scheduled session has been held with attendance taken.
steps.verify: Check the session schedule against held sessions; pass if each scheduled session occurred with an attendee list recorded.

steps.title: Document findings within 2 business days per session
steps.sop: The Business Analyst documents each session in the Confluence '<initiative>-current-state-discovery' space within 2 business days: attendee list, current-state process map, pain points with owner, and identified data sources, with the findings template fully populated. Done when every held session has a complete findings page.
steps.verify: Open each findings page in Confluence; pass if it was created within 2 business days of the session and all four template elements are populated.

steps.title: Tag high-impact pain points and scope triggers
steps.sop: The Business Analyst tags pain points affecting customer data, financial accuracy, or regulatory reporting as 'high-impact' for future-state prioritization; findings that materially change scope or reveal a new regulated data flow trigger a scope re-baseline and stakeholder review. Done when all qualifying items are tagged and any trigger is logged.
steps.verify: Filter findings by tag in Confluence; pass if every qualifying pain point carries 'high-impact' and any scope-changing finding links a re-baseline record.

steps.title: Validate volume claims against source-system counts
steps.sop: The Backend Developer validates every volume claim in the findings (e.g. transactions/day) against a source-system count rather than an estimate, citing the query used. Done when each claim carries a validated figure and source.
steps.verify: Open the findings' volume figures; pass if each cites a source-system count and the figure matches that source.

steps.title: Reconcile sessions to findings and log follow-ups
steps.sop: The Business Analyst reconciles held sessions to findings pages (count equal, 0 undocumented) and logs open questions or unvalidated findings as 'Discovery-Followup' items with owner and due date and a 5-business-day SLA; items unresolved past 5 business days escalate to the Product Owner. Done when the reconcile is 0-delta and all follow-ups are owned.
steps.verify: Compare session count to findings-page count and open the follow-up log; pass if counts match and every follow-up has owner, due date, and SLA status.

steps.title: Obtain SME sign-off on each findings page
steps.sop: The Business Analyst obtains sign-off from the session's SMEs on their findings page in Confluence. Done when every findings page carries SME sign-off.
steps.verify: Open each findings page; pass if an SME sign-off with name and date is recorded on 100% of pages.

steps.title: Complete the Tech Lead reasonableness check
steps.sop: The Tech Lead independently reviews the documented current-state maps and pain-point log for reasonableness. Done when the check is recorded with any challenges resolved.
steps.verify: Open the review record; pass if the Tech Lead check is logged and no unresolved challenge remains.

steps.title: Obtain Product Owner sign-off on the discovery outputs
steps.sop: The Product Owner signs off the documented current-state process maps and prioritized pain-point log in Confluence, versioned and timestamped, linked to the initiative epic. Done when the sign-off is recorded on the versioned findings.
steps.verify: Open the discovery findings page history; pass if the Product Owner sign-off references the current version and the page links to the initiative epic.

steps.title: Publish the quarterly CoP schedule in Confluence
steps.sop: The Software Engineer publishes the quarter's session schedule for each active CoP (Backend, Frontend, DevOps, Testing) on the CoP Confluence page, at a bi-weekly cadence of at least 6 sessions per CoP per quarter. Done when every active CoP has a dated schedule.
steps.verify: Open the CoP pages in Confluence; pass if each active CoP shows >=6 scheduled sessions for the quarter at the stated cadence.

steps.title: Facilitate each scheduled session
steps.sop: The Software Engineer (or the designated CoP facilitator) runs each session with a named topic, with the Backend Developer and UI Developer participating for their guilds. Done when the session is held as scheduled.
steps.verify: Check the session log against the schedule; pass if each scheduled session was held or has a logged cancellation.

steps.title: Record each session's required fields in Confluence
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records for each session in Confluence: date, CoP name, facilitator, topic, attendees, and a link to notes/recording — a session does not count as delivered without all six. Done when every held session has a complete record.
steps.verify: Open each session record in Confluence; pass if all six required fields are populated, including a working notes/recording link.

steps.title: Commit shared code samples to the source code/CI-CD repository
steps.sop: The Backend Developer commits reference code samples or patterns produced in sessions to the source code/CI-CD repository, linked from the session notes. Done when each session's shared code artifacts are committed and linked.
steps.verify: Follow the links from session notes; pass if each referenced sample resolves to a commit in the source code/CI-CD repository.

steps.title: Reconcile cadence and attendance for the quarter
steps.sop: The Software Engineer reconciles at quarter end: logged sessions >= planned cadence per CoP, and attendance reconciled against the CoP membership list, with the session log complete by quarter end. Done when the reconciliation is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the quarter reconciliation on the CoP dashboard page; pass if every CoP met its cadence and attendance figures tie to the membership list.

steps.title: Log missed sessions and escalate repeat misses
steps.sop: The Software Engineer logs missed/cancelled sessions as exceptions on the CoP page with reason and owner = CoP facilitator; two consecutive misses escalate to the Platform Engineering Lead with a recovery plan, and documentation gaps are assigned to the facilitator with a 5-business-day fix SLA. Done when every miss has an owned exception.
steps.verify: Open the exception entries; pass if each miss shows reason and owner, and any two-in-a-row miss links a Platform Engineering Lead escalation with recovery plan.

steps.title: Obtain Tech Lead sign-off on the quarter's session log
steps.sop: The Tech Lead reviews and signs off the quarter's session log in Confluence; notes/recordings are retained for the current plus prior year. Done when the sign-off is recorded with 100% of held sessions documented.
steps.verify: Open the session log; pass if the Tech Lead sign-off is present and every held session has notes and attendance captured.

steps.title: Schedule the retro within 3 business days of sprint close
steps.sop: The Scrum Master schedules a retrospective for every squad that closed a sprint in the period — one retro per squad per sprint — within 3 business days of sprint close. Done when each closed sprint has a scheduled retro.
steps.verify: Compare closed sprints to scheduled retros; pass if every closed sprint shows a retro dated within 3 business days of its close.

steps.title: Facilitate the retrospective session
steps.sop: The Software Engineer facilitates the session with the squad (Backend Developer, UI Developer, Scrum Master), collecting at least 3 'what went well' items and at least 3 'what to improve' items. Done when both lists meet the minimum.
steps.verify: Review the session output; pass if >=3 went-well and >=3 improve items were captured with the attendee list.

steps.title: Record the retro on the Confluence template page
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records the retro on the Confluence retro page using the template columns Went Well / Improve / Action / Owner / Due, including sprint id and attendees, with at least 1 action item carrying an owner and due date. Done when the page is complete per template.
steps.verify: Open the retro page in Confluence; pass if all template columns are populated, sprint id and attendees appear, and >=1 action item has owner and due date.

steps.title: Reconcile retros held against closed sprints
steps.sop: The Scrum Master reconciles the count of retros held to the count of squads with a closed sprint in the period. Done when the variance is 0.
steps.verify: Compare the sprint-report squad count to the retro-record count; pass if the counts match with 0 variance.

steps.title: Track action-item closure into the next sprint
steps.sop: The Scrum Master tracks carry-over action items; at least 70% of the prior retro's action items must be closed by the next sprint's end. Done when closure tracking is recorded on the retro page.
steps.verify: Open the action-item tracker; pass if closure of carried-over items is >=70% or a recovery note explains the shortfall.

steps.title: Log skipped retros as SDLC-Exception
steps.sop: The Scrum Master logs any squad that skipped a retro as an 'SDLC-Exception' with reason and a make-up date within 5 business days (owner = Scrum Master). Done when every skip has an exception with a make-up date.
steps.verify: Open the exception log; pass if each skipped retro shows reason, Scrum Master ownership, and a make-up date inside 5 business days.

steps.title: Obtain Tech Lead sign-off with retention set
steps.sop: The Tech Lead signs off the period's retro compliance; Confluence page versions are retained 24 months in the team space. Done when 100% of closed sprints have a completed retro record with owned, dated action items.
steps.verify: Open the compliance summary; pass if the Tech Lead sign-off is recorded, every closed sprint links a completed retro page, and retention is marked 24 months.

steps.title: Prepare the workshop from the approved template
steps.sop: The Software Engineer prepares the session using the standard requirements-workshop template v-current from the BA playbook, agreed with the Product Owner before the session; scope = the epic's stories plus the impacted Guidewire and integration touchpoints named in the epic charter, within the current PI's elaboration window. Done when the template version and scope are agreed and recorded.
steps.verify: Open the workshop preparation record; pass if it cites the template version, the Product Owner's pre-session agreement, and the charter's scope items.

steps.title: Run the elicitation workshop
steps.sop: The Business Analyst facilitates the workshop with business stakeholders and SMEs, capturing the attendee list and decisions; the Backend Developer and UI Developer probe technical feasibility. Done when the session is held with attendees and decisions captured.
steps.verify: Review the workshop outputs; pass if the attendee list and a decision record exist for the session.

steps.title: Log every requirement in the requirements repository
steps.sop: The Business Analyst logs each captured requirement in the requirements repository with unique ID, business rationale, INVEST-compliant story text, testable Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, MoSCoW priority, and a named business owner. Done when every requirement carries all six elements.
steps.verify: Open the logged requirements in the requirements repository; pass if 100% show ID, rationale, story text, Given/When/Then criteria, priority, and business owner.

steps.title: Flag incomplete stories as Needs Refinement
steps.sop: The Business Analyst flags stories missing acceptance criteria as 'Needs Refinement' in the requirements repository, excluding them from ready-for-dev, and schedules a follow-up refinement session within 5 business days (owner = Business Analyst). Done when no criteria-less story sits in a ready state.
steps.verify: Query ready-for-dev items; pass if none lacks acceptance criteria and each flagged story shows a follow-up session within 5 business days.

steps.title: Obtain second confirmation on high-impact requirements
steps.sop: The Business Analyst routes requirements touching pricing, underwriting rules, or claims payout logic — flagged 'high-impact' — for a second SME confirmation and Solution Architect review before acceptance. Done when every high-impact item shows both confirmations.
steps.verify: Filter high-impact requirements in the requirements repository; pass if each shows the second SME confirmation and the Solution Architect review recorded.

steps.title: Escalate oversized or cross-system requirements
steps.sop: The Software Engineer escalates any requirement estimated above 8 story points or crossing more than 2 systems to the Product Owner and Architecture for scope/feasibility sign-off before commit. Done when every qualifying item carries that sign-off.
steps.verify: Filter requirements >8 points or >2 systems; pass if each shows Product Owner + Architecture sign-off prior to commitment.

steps.title: Reconcile the traceability matrix
steps.sop: The Business Analyst reconciles the requirement count in the requirements repository to the workshop notes and the traceability matrix (delta = 0), with each requirement mapping to at least one business objective and 0 orphan stories. Done when the matrix reconciles completely.
steps.verify: Open the traceability matrix; pass if counts match the workshop notes exactly, every requirement maps to a business objective, and no orphan exists.

steps.title: Log open items in the decision log
steps.sop: The Software Engineer logs open questions and conflicting requirements as 'req-open-item' entries with owner and due date, and records parked items in the decision log with a disposition before stories are marked ready. Done when no open item is untracked.
steps.verify: Open the decision log and open-item list; pass if every question/conflict has owner + due date and every parked item shows a disposition.

steps.title: Obtain Product Owner sign-off on the workshop outputs
steps.sop: The Product Owner signs off the workshop notes and requirement set (retained minimum 3 years with version and timestamp), after the Business Analyst's independent re-performance check. Done when PASS criteria hold: 100% of committed stories have testable Given/When/Then criteria, a business owner, and traceability to a business objective.
steps.verify: Open the sign-off record in the requirements repository; pass if the Product Owner approval is recorded on the versioned outputs and no committed story lacks criteria or owner.

steps.title: Define the evidence checklist for the epic
steps.sop: The Software Engineer defines the evidence checklist for the release epic (e.g. EPIC-1420): 1 architecture diagram + N code-review records (N = merged PRs in the epic) + 1 CI test-result set + 1 risk-log export, covering only the window from feature-branch cut to release-candidate freeze (e.g. 2026-06-15 through 2026-06-30) — evidence dated outside the window is excluded. Done when the checklist with the expected control total is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the checklist; pass if it lists the four artifact types, computes N from the epic's merged-PR count, and states the in-scope date window.

steps.title: Collect the versioned architecture diagram
steps.sop: The Solutions Architect collects the current C4 architecture diagram for the release with its version tag. Done when the diagram carries a version tag, author, and timestamp inside the review window.
steps.verify: Open the collected diagram; pass if the version tag is present and its date falls within the release window.

steps.title: Export the code-review records from the source code/CI-CD repository
steps.sop: The Software Engineer exports the code-review record for every merged PR in the epic from the source code/CI-CD repository. Done when each record shows 2 approvers, a permalink, author, timestamp, and the Jira issue key.
steps.verify: Open the exported records; pass if the record count equals the epic's merged-PR count and each shows 2 approvers plus the four metadata fields.

steps.title: Export the CI test-result artifact
steps.sop: The Backend Developer exports the CI test-result set for the release candidate from the source code/CI-CD repository. Done when the artifact shows the pass rate and coverage percentage for the RC build.
steps.verify: Open the test-result artifact; pass if it is keyed to the RC build and displays both pass rate and coverage %.

steps.title: Export the risk log from the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC)
steps.sop: The Software Engineer exports the release's risk log from the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC). Done when the export is dated within the review window and covers the epic's scope.
steps.verify: Open the risk-log export; pass if it covers the epic, is timestamped within the window, and matches the current GRC risk register for the release.

steps.title: Validate metadata on every evidence item
steps.sop: The Software Engineer validates each item against the assurance-checklist data dictionary fields (artifact_type, source_url, author, timestamp, jira_key, version, approver_count); any blank field means the item is rejected and re-collected. Done when every item passes field validation.
steps.verify: Check each evidence row; pass if all seven dictionary fields are populated and no rejected item remains in the bundle.

steps.title: Reconcile the bundle and log gaps as SDLC-Exception
steps.sop: The Software Engineer reconciles the evidence count to the control total (merged-PR count + 3 fixed non-PR artifacts) with delta = 0; missing or stale evidence is raised as an 'SDLC-Exception' (assignee = Engineering Manager) with disposition waiver/remediate/accept-risk and a 10-business-day remediation SLA. Done when the reconcile balances or every gap has an owned exception.
steps.verify: Compare the bundle count to the control total; pass if delta = 0, or each gap links an exception with assignee, disposition, and SLA date.

steps.title: Upload the bundle to the GRC platform with the prior-release comparison
steps.sop: The Software Engineer uploads the evidence bundle to the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC) under /assurance/<epic-key>/ with immutable timestamp and version label v<n> (retention 3 years per the NYDFS audit-trail requirement), attaching the pre/post comparison against the prior release bundle showing all mandatory artifact types present and no regression in coverage or open-risk count, cross-linked to the release change ticket. Done when the bundle and comparison are stored.
steps.verify: Open /assurance/<epic-key>/ in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC); pass if the v<n> bundle exists with immutable timestamp, 3-year retention, the comparison report, and the change-ticket link.

steps.title: Obtain Tech Lead sign-off on the evidence set
steps.sop: The Tech Lead reviews the complete bundle and signs off. Done when PASS criteria hold: all 4 mandatory artifact types present, each with valid version/timestamp and required approvals, 0 items missing — any absence blocks the assurance gate pending remediation or an approved waiver.
steps.verify: Open the sign-off record; pass if the Tech Lead approval is recorded and the census check shows no absent, unversioned, or unapproved artifact.

steps.title: Elicit requirements into the requirements repository
steps.sop: The Software Engineer elicits functional and non-functional requirements with the Product Owner and named SMEs during the elaboration window, capturing them in the requirements repository register for the epic. Done when the register covers the feature's intake scope before stories enter 'Ready for Dev'.
steps.verify: Open the epic's register in the requirements repository; pass if every intake-scope requirement is captured with its source stakeholder noted.

steps.title: Create stories with acceptance criteria in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps
steps.sop: The Business Analyst creates each story under the epic in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps with the fields: Summary, Description (user-story statement), Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then in the custom field), Epic Link, and links to the SME source docs. Done when every story carries all five fields.
steps.verify: Open the epic's stories in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; pass if each shows the user-story statement, testable Given/When/Then criteria, epic link, and source-doc links.

steps.title: Reconcile stories to the requirements register
steps.sop: The Business Analyst reconciles the Jira story count for the epic against the requirements register row count in the requirements repository. Done when the count of agreed stories equals the count of scoped requirements with 0 unmapped items.
steps.verify: Compare the register row count to the story count in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; pass if they match and every register row maps to a story.

steps.title: Log clarifications and escalate aging items
steps.sop: The Software Engineer logs ambiguous or contested requirements as 'Clarification' sub-tasks in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps with owner and due date, assigned to the Business Analyst when gaps surface during dev; unresolved items block 'Ready for Dev' and are raised as 'SDLC-Exception' to the Product Owner if aging more than 5 business days. Done when no ambiguity is untracked.
steps.verify: Query 'Clarification' sub-tasks; pass if each has owner and due date, blocked stories are not in 'Ready for Dev', and any item older than 5 business days shows the escalated exception.

steps.title: Run the Business Analyst INVEST check
steps.sop: The Business Analyst applies the INVEST criteria at refinement to every story in the epic intended for the upcoming sprints. Done when each story passes INVEST or is returned with the failing criterion noted.
steps.verify: Open the refinement record; pass if every sprint-bound story shows an INVEST pass or a documented return.

steps.title: Obtain Product Owner sign-off on every sprint-bound story
steps.sop: The Product Owner signs off each story entering the sprint in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps — the Product Owner is the authorized approver per the delegation matrix (Business Analyst as named backup, reviewed each PI). Done when 100% of stories entering the sprint have PO-approved, testable acceptance criteria.
steps.verify: Open the sprint-bound stories; pass if every one shows the Product Owner (or documented backup) approval and none lacks acceptance criteria.

steps.title: Retain the requirements evidence
steps.sop: The Software Engineer confirms the requirements page versions in the requirements repository and the Jira story history are retained for the project lifetime + 24 months. Done when the retention marking is in place on both records.
steps.verify: Open the register version history and a sample story history; pass if both are intact and marked for project-lifetime + 24-month retention.

tasks.taskName: Generate and validate API reference documentation

steps.title: Regenerate the API specs in the source code/CI-CD repository
steps.sop: The Software Engineer regenerates the versioned OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification in the source code/CI-CD repository on merge to develop, covering every REST/event endpoint of the services shipping in this release plus the SDK/interface guides. Done when the spec builds from the current merge.
steps.verify: Open the spec-generation job in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if the spec regenerated on the latest merge and includes every in-scope service.

steps.title: Complete every endpoint's reference entry
steps.sop: The Backend Developer ensures every documented endpoint in the source code/CI-CD repository lists method, path, auth scheme, request/response schema, error codes, and at least one worked example. Done when no endpoint entry is missing any of the six elements.
steps.verify: Sample endpoint entries in the generated reference; pass if each shows all six elements including a runnable worked example.

steps.title: Pass the Spectral lint gate
steps.sop: The Software Engineer runs Spectral against the spec in the source code/CI-CD repository. Done when the linter reports 0 errors and 0 missing-description warnings.
steps.verify: Open the Spectral output in CI; pass if errors = 0 and missing-description warnings = 0.

steps.title: Run the docs-sync drift check in CI
steps.sop: The Backend Developer runs the automated docs-sync diff in the source code/CI-CD repository comparing the endpoint count in the generated spec to the routes registered in code. Done when the counts are equal — any drift fails the 'docs-sync' pipeline stage.
steps.verify: Open the 'docs-sync' stage result; pass if the stage is green with spec endpoints = registered routes.

steps.title: Log gaps as DOC-Gap tickets
steps.sop: The Software Engineer logs every undocumented or mismatched endpoint as a 'DOC-Gap' ticket with owner = Software Engineer and a fix-by-release-cut SLA. Done when no known gap lacks a ticket.
steps.verify: Open the DOC-Gap ticket list; pass if each drift/mismatch from the checks has a ticket with the owner and release-cut deadline.

steps.title: Validate the reference against the release-candidate build
steps.sop: The Integration Engineer validates accuracy in the release-candidate build before go-live by exercising the documented worked examples against the RC endpoints. Done when every sampled example behaves as documented.
steps.verify: Review the RC validation record; pass if the exercised examples returned the documented responses with no mismatch left unticketed.

steps.title: Publish the doc bundle to Confluence
steps.sop: The Software Engineer publishes the validated doc bundle to Confluence tagged with the release version and git SHA; superseded versions are archived, not deleted. Done when the bundle is live with page history intact.
steps.verify: Open the published bundle in Confluence; pass if it carries the release version + git SHA tag and prior versions remain accessible in the archive.

steps.title: Obtain Tech Lead sign-off on the validated docs
steps.sop: The Tech Lead reviews the validated reference documentation and signs off before go-live. Done when the approval is recorded against the published release version.
steps.verify: Open the sign-off record; pass if the Tech Lead approval references the published bundle's release version and predates go-live.

steps.title: Author the API design standard in Confluence
steps.sop: The Integration Architect authors/updates the enterprise API design standard in Confluence covering all internal and partner-facing HTTP APIs, mandating: OpenAPI 3.0 spec required, RESTful resource-oriented design, RFC 7807 error format, URI versioning for breaking changes, OAuth 2.0/OIDC auth, pagination for collections, and no PII in URLs. Done when the standard documents all seven mandates.
steps.verify: Open the standard in Confluence; pass if all seven mandated rules are stated and the document carries its v<major.minor> version.

steps.title: Encode every rule as a Spectral check in the ruleset repo
steps.sop: The Integration Engineer encodes each rule of the standard as a Spectral lint check in the git/api-standards ruleset in the source code/CI-CD repository, versioned with tags. Done when every rule in the standard has a corresponding lint check.
steps.verify: Open the ruleset in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if each of the standard's rules maps to a Spectral check and the ruleset is tagged to the standard version.

steps.title: Enable the Spectral CI gate on all API repos
steps.sop: The Software Engineer enables the Spectral gate in the CI pipelines of the source code/CI-CD repository for 100% of API repos. Done when every API repo's pipeline runs the current ruleset as a blocking gate.
steps.verify: Check the pipeline configs across API repos; pass if the Spectral gate is active and blocking on 100% of them with the current ruleset version.

steps.title: Reconcile the gateway API catalog to the developer portal
steps.sop: The Backend Developer reconciles the published API catalog (Azure API Management governance policies) against the developer portal so every published API has a governed spec entry. Done when there are 0 orphans on either side.
steps.verify: Compare the gateway catalog to the portal listing; pass if every published API shows a governed spec entry and the orphan count is 0.

steps.title: Take the standard through ARB quarterly review
steps.sop: The Integration Architect presents the standard at the API guild / ARB quarterly review; the standard is effective from its publication date v<major.minor> and re-versioned on change, with each ARB approval recorded with date and version. Done when the current version carries an ARB approval record.
steps.verify: Open the approval log; pass if the current standard version shows an ARB approval with date, and any change since triggered a re-version.

steps.title: Log deviations as ARB-Exception tickets
steps.sop: The Integration Architect ensures every deviation from the standard is logged as an 'ARB-Exception' ticket with justification, compensating control, and expiry, recorded in the architecture decision log. Done when no known deviation lacks a ticket.
steps.verify: Open the architecture decision log; pass if each deviation links an 'ARB-Exception' with all three elements and an unexpired or renewed expiry date.

steps.title: Obtain Enterprise Architect sign-off on publication
steps.sop: The Enterprise Architect signs off the published standard in Confluence, whose page history retains all versions, and the tagged ruleset in the source code/CI-CD repository. Done when the sign-off is recorded against the published version.
steps.verify: Open the standard's page history in Confluence; pass if the Enterprise Architect sign-off is on the current version and the referenced ruleset tag exists in the source code/CI-CD repository.
